system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

**Basis:** AUD 24 million for 100% of Paperbark Analytics, debt-free/cash-free, under NSW law. The Seller’s “[STANDARD]”, “FINAL” and “agreed” labels do **not** establish Buyer agreement. The recommendations below are Buyer negotiating positions, not assertions of market practice. The underlying DD documents and complete SPA have not been provided.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Reopen; seek 100% of price as the Buyer’s opening position**, with any concession assessed against diligence and available security/insurance—20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds; a tipping basket; aggregation of related claims; appropriate exclusions for special claim categories. | **Seek AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated—the proposed combination can exclude significant cumulative losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties; separate periods for other categories; timely notified claims preserved. | **Seek 36 months, with 24 months a potential negotiated fallback**, and reject automatic application to all Claims—18 months may not expose issues across sufficient reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate, strong warranties covering capacity, ownership, valid issuance, all shares and freedom from encumbrances; no general thresholds. | **Require a separate regime: at least a 100%-of-price cap and a substantially longer claim period**, settled against applicable limitation rules—the Buyer must have meaningful recourse if it does not acquire the promised shares. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is identified. | Express preservation of fraud/fraudulent misrepresentation remedies, including relevant attribution to the Seller; preservation of non-excludable rights. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure, knowledge and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance restrictions**, with NSW counsel checking enforceability—the Seller should not contractually shield fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public corporate records. | Only fair disclosure, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; a fixed, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket disclosure; require specific warranty-linked disclosures**, tightly define any permitted general disclosures and preserve an indexed snapshot—document availability is not equivalent to meaningful disclosure of a liability. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from data room/public records. | Delete the qualifier; alternatively, tightly limited actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without constructive knowledge or adviser imputation. | **Delete; if conceded, restrict to actual, conscious knowledge of the relevant facts and breach by named individuals**—the current drafting converts diligence access into a sweeping loss of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfaction of its conditions. | A genuine condition precedent requiring effective consent and satisfaction of associated conditions, without materially adverse changes. | **Require final consent complying with clauses 11.2–11.3, evidence of conditions satisfied, and Buyer-controlled waiver**—written consent alone may not protect a customer representing approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Verified payout, discharge of all relevant security and guarantees, and compliance with change-control requirements at Completion. | **Make repayment and effective discharge simultaneous Completion requirements**, using an agreed lender payout/release mechanism and correct debt adjustment—post-Completion promises are inconsistent with a debt-free acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller calls them its responsibility. On-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, without leaving the Company underfunded. | **Quantify and include them in the Completion mechanics as Seller-funded costs or a price deduction, backed by an indemnity**, without double counting—calling them Seller costs does not ensure payment or protect the acquired Company. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, without independent proof of non-payment, payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment status and complete ownership/licensing rights for all relevant materials; protection against associated title and infringement losses. | **Require payment evidence and an effective confirmatory assignment at or before Completion; broaden the indemnity beyond the invoice**, with an appropriate separate cap and duration—the payment amount does not measure the potential loss from missing IP rights. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; possible export of approximately **1,240 records**, with access, scope and notification obligations unresolved. | Prompt independent investigation, containment and legal assessment; visibility over remediation and lawful notifications; allocation of pre-Completion incident risk. | **Require investigation deliverables and a tailored indemnity for resulting lawful liabilities, response costs and third-party claims**, considering retention or a Completion condition if material unresolved risk remains—uncertainty is neither proof of a breach nor grounds to dismiss exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Verification of combined scope, timing, commercial benefit, accruals, cancellation rights and any unusual commitments. | **Review DD-008 and DD-011 together before classification; apply ordinary-course covenants and adjust only where justified by agreed accounting/debt-like definitions**—neither automatic acceptance nor automatic treatment as debt is supported. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to every Claim unless expressly excluded. | Distinct treatment of general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price/debt adjustments, covenants and fraud. | **Replace the blanket override with an express category-by-category liability matrix and clear precedence provisions**—otherwise general limitations may silently defeat specifically negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s share register showing Harbourglass as holder of 100%. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options/conversion rights and transfer restrictions, plus valid transfer deliverables. | **Verify the register against corporate records, issue/transfer documents and relevant searches; require certificates or appropriate replacements, releases and transfer registration**—the register is important evidence, not complete assurance of unencumbered ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP said to be settled under the general liability regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax and suitable statutory-period coverage; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties, including contractor-created IP. | **Keep both open: negotiate standalone tax protection and tailored IP scope, caps and periods, preserving the Ironquay indemnity separately**—tax and core software ownership risks should not default to an 18-month, 20% general-warranty remedy. |

**Priority before signing:** resolve Bluefen conditionality, Riverlark discharge mechanics, bonus funding, Ironquay ownership evidence and the incident investigation; then ensure the liability and disclosure provisions do not neutralise those protections.
=== END ADVICE ===
